children: India's Nifty Bank index, an index comprising of 14 major banks in the country, hit a record high of 62,442 on Tuesday, November 17, surpassing its previous high of 61,764 made in February this year. On the flip side, banks in the US are close to flashing a bearish signal.

The US KBW Bank Index fell 2% on Tuesday, and is now nearing a potential and rare "death cross" technical pattern on the charts, which indicates bearish momentum. In technical terminologies, a "death cross" is formed when the 50-Day Moving Average of an index or a stock, breaks below its 200-Day Moving Average.

Such a pattern is closely watched as it generally indicates more weakness, at least in the short-term. Banking shares in the US, having peaked in August, are worried over business disruptions and rising borrowing costs. Disruptions to services across large banks impacted customers over the weekend.

A highly classified network that the National Security Agency uses for its internal communications also went down on Tuesday, triggering further selling in banking stocks, that were already under pressure after JPMorgan faced a disruption to its own systems, sending the stock lower.

Quarterly results reported by banks in the US were also mixed on worries of how AI will impact the financial services space, and what steps will the US Federal Reserve take to combat the persistent inflationary pressures.

The KBW Bank Index, which comprises of 24 stocks, last made a "death cross" on the charts back in April 2025, triggered by the Liberation day announcements made by US President Donald Trump. The index has formed this pattern eight times in the last 10 years, and is usually associated with an extraordinary event, such as the 2023 banking crisis or tariffs.
Shares of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are down more than 15% each from their respective record highs in August, while those of JPMorgan are down close to 10% from the top.

title: Nifty Bank is at a record high, but the US banking index is flashing a 'bearish' signal
